facts.fact_text: The applicants participated in an assembly on 6 May 2014.
According to the applicants, they were among people who gathered near the Baku Assize Court on 6 May 2014 to support members of Nida (an opposition group) who were being tried on that day.
The courtroom of the Baku Assize Court was full on 6 May 2014, and therefore some people gathered outside the court to wait for the outcome of the proceedings.
When the Baku Assize Court announced its judgment on 6 May 2014, those who had gathered outside began to protest against the judgment, considering it unfair.
According to the applicants, the protest on 6 May 2014 near the Baku Assize Court was brief, spontaneous and peaceful.
Immediately after the protesters started chanting slogans on 6 May 2014, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the demonstration near the Baku Assize Court.
The applicants were arrested during the dispersal operation on 6 May 2014.
On 6 May 2014, the day of the applicants' arrest, administrative-offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued against the applicants.

The administrative-offence reports issued against the applicants stated that they had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan: participation in a public assembly organised not in accordance with the law.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the second applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to a period of administrative detention of thirty days.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the second applicant to a period of administrative detention of twenty days.

The administrative-offence reports issued against the applicants stated that they had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan: participation in a public assembly organised not in accordance with the law.
At the time of the applicants' arrest, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of Azerbaijan of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats (AZN).
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced, for the first time, punishments in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days or community service for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, fixing the amounts as follows: between AZN 300 and AZN 600 for participants of an assembly; AZN 1,500 to AZN 3,000 for individuals who organise an assembly; AZN 3,000 to AZN 6,000 for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly; and between AZN 15,000 and AZN 30,000 for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.

By Law no. 651-IVQD of 14 May 2013, which entered into force on 5 June 2013, the administrative detention sentence provided for in Article 298.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan was increased to 'up to two months'.

By Law no. 651-IVQD of 14 May 2013, which entered into force on 5 June 2013, the administrative detention sentence provided for in Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan was increased to 'up to two months'.
According to the applicants, the protest on 6 May 2014 near the Baku Assize Court was brief, spontaneous and peaceful.
Immediately after the protesters started chanting slogans on 6 May 2014, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the demonstration near the Baku Assize Court.
The applicants were arrested during the dispersal operation on 6 May 2014.
After their arrest, the applicants were taken to a police station.
The applicants were kept overnight at the police station.
The applicants were questioned at the police station.
According to the applicants, they were never served with copies of the administrative-offence reports issued against them.
According to the applicants, they were never served with copies of other documents from their case files.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer while they were in police custody.
According to a police officer's decision and an order dated 6 May 2014, a State-funded lawyer, Mr O.A., was invited to defend the first applicant.
According to a police officer's decision and an order dated 6 May 2014, a State-funded lawyer, Mr A.B., was invited to defend the second applicant.
The applicants were brought before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014, the day following their arrest.
According to the applicants, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court (first-instance court) was very brief in the case of the first applicant.
According to the applicants, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court (first-instance court) was very brief in the case of the second applicant.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Nasimi District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing before the Nasimi District Court.
A State-funded lawyer, Mr O.A., was invited to defend the first applicant before the Nasimi District Court.

The State-funded lawyer invited to defend the first applicant before the Nasimi District Court, Mr O.A., was the same lawyer who had been invited to defend her in accordance with the police officer's decision of 6 May 2014.
The second applicant was not represented by a lawyer before the Nasimi District Court.

According to the transcript of the hearing before the Nasimi District Court in the second applicant's case, the second applicant refused the assistance of the State-funded lawyer and decided to defend himself in person.
According to the transcript of the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant, the State-funded lawyer Mr O.A. did not make any oral or written submissions.

The only witnesses questioned during the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant were police officers who, according to official records, had arrested her or issued the administrative-offence report on her.
The police officers questioned as witnesses during the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant testified that the first applicant had staged an unauthorised protest.
With respect to the second applicant, the Nasimi District Court did not question any witness.

According to the transcript of the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant, the first applicant stated that she had participated in the protest of 6 May 2014 and had rightfully used 'improper language' in the course of the protest.

According to the transcript of the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the second applicant, the second applicant stated that he had simply protested against an unfair judgment against the Nida members and had not committed any unlawful action.
The Nasimi District Court found that the first applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
The Nasimi District Court found that the second applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
On unspecified dates, the applicants lodged appeals with the Baku Court of Appeal against their convictions by the Nasimi District Court.

In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants argued that their convictions had been in violation of their rights because the protest in which they had participated had been spontaneous and peaceful.
In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants complained that their arrests had been unlawful.
In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants complained that the hearings before the Nasimi District Court had not been fair.
The applicants asked the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the Nasimi District Court's decisions in their respective cases.
The first applicant was assisted by a lawyer of her own choosing before the Baku Court of Appeal.
The second applicant was not represented by a lawyer before the Baku Court of Appeal.
On 16 May 2014, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the first applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court in her case.
On 22 May 2014, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the second applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court in his case.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', stated that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment in Azerbaijan requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.
Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe raised concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations.
Report CommDH(2013)14 was issued on 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

In Report CommDH(2013)14, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

In Report CommDH(2013)14, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed under the amended laws, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations in Azerbaijan.

In Report CommDH(2013)14, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in a demonstration, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

In Report CommDH(2013)14, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.

A summary of other relevant domestic provisions concerning administrative proceedings and the organisation and holding of public assemblies in Azerbaijan, and relevant extracts from international documents, can be found in the judgment in the case of Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, paragraphs 27-42, 15 October 2015).
